rows: Whether Europa Clipper is a life-detection mission
Clipper can constrain ocean/ice chemistry; it is not designed to prove life.
Whether Titan organic chemistry implies biology
Amino acids or organics are not enough; chirality/context would matter.
Whether Mars evidence needs Earth labs
MSR science is high value but program architecture and cost remain unsettled.
Whether Enceladus can be tested directly
Decadal priority is not a launch guarantee; contamination and payload design are decisive.
Whether Venus clouds deserve biosignature follow-up
DAVINCI+ atmospheric history and aerosol context
Cloud chemistry may be habitable-ish, but water activity and acidity remain severe constraints.
Whether exoplanet biosignatures need a future flagship
Remote atmospheric biosignatures will be probabilistic, not instant proof.
